title: Sell Mineral Rights in McRae, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in McRae, AR
metaDescription: McRae, AR mineral rights in White County's Fayetteville Shale gas trend near Searcy. Legacy leases from the 2000s boom, now in long-tail decline.
heroLead: McRae is a small White County town where nearly every long-held family tract carries some connection to the Fayetteville Shale leasing wave that swept through the county in the 2000s.
intro: White County's role as a core Fayetteville Shale county means McRae-area land saw significant leasing and drilling activity during the play's peak years. Many local mineral interests have a production history stretching back over a decade, now settled into the low, steady decline typical of mature shale gas wells.

sections.heading: A County That Drilled Hard, Then Slowed
paragraphs: The pace of new drilling across White County, including around McRae, has been minimal for years compared to the boom period, as low natural gas prices made new horizontal wells less economical. Existing wells have largely kept producing, but new development on undrilled tracts has mostly stalled, which is worth understanding before assuming an unleased interest here will see near-term activity.

sections.heading: What to Do With an Old Lease
paragraphs: If your McRae-area mineral rights have been under the same lease since the 2000s, it's worth confirming whether that lease is still being held by production or has lapsed. An expired lease means your rights are effectively unleased and open, which changes how a buyer would approach valuing them compared to a producing interest.

faqs.question: Why hasn't there been new drilling near McRae in years?
faqs.answer: Low natural gas prices since the mid-2010s have made new Fayetteville Shale wells less economically attractive compared to the boom years, so activity across White County, including near McRae, has slowed considerably.

faqs.question: How can I tell if my old lease is still valid?
faqs.answer: A lease is typically held by production as long as a well on the covering unit keeps producing. We can check your lease and unit status against county and Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission records.

faqs.question: Does a smaller, declining royalty check mean my interest is worth less to a buyer?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily on its own. A buyer looks at the full production history and remaining reserves, not only the most recent check, to arrive at a fair valuation.

faqs.question: What paperwork should I gather before contacting a buyer about my McRae interest?
faqs.answer: Your most recent royalty statement or division order if you have one, your legal description, and any lease document referencing the tract. Missing pieces can usually be located through county records.

faqs.question: Is it common for owners near McRae to not realize their lease has expired?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's a common surprise, since a lease can lapse quietly once a well is plugged, and nothing formally notifies the mineral owner unless they check.
